dangerous_cpts.main_problem: The same CVP parameter is activated in all repeated failure scenarios and in no reported success scenarios, which makes it the most failure-specific candidate in the common reasoning path. Semantically, CVP is a downstream observable of LVEDVOLUME, so it may be contributing to incorrect predictions by mapping the implicated ventricular filling state too strongly away from HIGH CVP.

suspicious_parameters.justification: Column 1 corresponds to LVEDVOLUME=NORMAL. In all six failures, the model assigns only 0.01 to CVP=HIGH under this parent state, and this exact parameter is not reported in successes. Because CVP is a clinical measurement that can vary even when filling volume is normal, this very small probability may be too restrictive and could help produce repeated mismatches.

dangerous_cpts.main_problem: BP lies at the end of the cardiovascular reasoning chain and combines CO with TPR. The implicated parameter appears in all six failures with a noticeably weaker success contrast than most upstream candidates, suggesting that the BP mapping itself may be part of the repeated error pattern rather than merely inheriting upstream activations.

suspicious_parameters.justification: Column 7 corresponds to CO=HIGH and TPR=NORMAL. The model deterministically favors BP=HIGH with probability 0.75. Physiologically, high cardiac output with normal peripheral resistance does not always imply high arterial pressure, so this mapping may be somewhat too strong and could plausibly contribute to repeated overprediction of high BP.

cpt_danger_report.overall_summary: Most candidates in the common failure pattern are heavily shared with successful scenarios and are better interpreted as upstream context rather than independently suspicious CPTs. CVP stands out because its activated parameter is failure-specific and clinically may be too restrictive. BP is also a plausible refinement candidate because it is the terminal prediction in the cardiovascular path and its HIGH assignment under high CO with normal TPR may be overly strong. No candidate is supported strongly enough for high or high_medium risk.
